A long walk along the coast

We set off at first light. The tide was out.

Gulls argued over the sand. A dog chased them.

The path climbed to the cliff top. Wind pushed at our coats.

At noon we ate bread and cheese. The sea was grey and calm.

A ferry crossed the bay. Its horn sounded twice.

We turned inland at the old mill. The lane was muddy.

Rain came in the afternoon. We sheltered in a barn.

By evening the sky had cleared. We walked home tired.

The lighthouse lamp came on. We watched it turn.

Supper was soup by the fire. Then we slept.
